name: 2.5D parallax photo
one_line: A still split into depth layers that drift at different rates under a virtual camera
summary: A photograph becomes a shallow stage: foreground, subject and background slide past each other as the camera moves, so a still gains depth and life. It suits slow reveals and establishing shots. Weak cut-outs, wrongly ordered planes and unpainted gaps behind the subject show as soon as the move widens.

routes.one_line: Segment the subject, build alpha layers, then move planes under a Three.js camera

steps.does: Separate subject from background with a segmentation mask
Cut the still into alpha layers and prepare the background behind the subject
Place layers at depths and move a camera across them

limits: Segmentation evidence is one portrait model on one image; hair and soft edges are unproven
Compositing evidence is a plain layer composite; clean-plate filling is not covered
No fixture moves layers at depth under a camera

routes.one_line: Segment and layer the still, then translate flat layers at depth-scaled rates in PixiJS

steps.does: Separate subject from background with a segmentation mask
Cut the still into alpha layers and prepare the background behind the subject
Move each layer at a rate set by its depth, from t

limits: PixiJS evidence covers Graphics geometry only; textured sprites are untested
Segmentation evidence is one portrait model on one image; hair and soft edges are unproven
Flat translation gives no perspective or scale change between planes

source: references/image-direction §5.4, references/motion-director §6; tool records as of 2026-11-20
